answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake if independent audits show fabricated work or collusion. One attacker can still create many names, but each name ties up capital and risks losing it; splitting a stake across a swarm does not multiply the total voting or job capacity. Auditors must be sampled unpredictably, so a falcon agent cannot quietly steer every check toward its own island harbor of linked identities.
